clue.text: Nightmare for young reporter kidnapped by Greek character in island

parts.note: I is the standard abbreviation for island; it opens the outer shell

indicators.note: someone kidnapped is held captive inside, so one piece is enclosed by the next
one thing sitting in another means the first is placed inside the second

parts.note: nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet
a cub reporter is a junior journalist
the second half of the abbreviation IS, closing the shell

explanation.surface: A junior journalist is snatched by a Greek on an island, which is a nightmare for the poor youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a double nesting: the island abbreviation is split open to hold the Greek letter, which itself holds the young reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: An incubus is a demon thought to lie upon sleepers, and by extension an oppressive dream or burden.

clue.text: Refrigerated salad ingredients?

parts.note: surface reading: salad vegetables kept cold in the fridge
setter's reading: a variety of lettuce whose name suggests frozen floating ice

explanation.surface: Someone is describing the chilled greens for a salad.
explanation.walkthrough: Any chilled lettuce is refrigerated; the question mark hints that one variety is named after a chunk of polar ice.
explanation.definitionFit: This crisp, pale variety of lettuce is a common salad base and takes its name from frozen ocean ice.

clue.text: Cash on delivery — a German analgesic drug

parts.note: COD is the standard abbreviation for cash on delivery
eine is the German for 'a' (feminine)

explanation.surface: A painkiller ordered by post from Germany, paid for at the door.
explanation.definitionFit: Codeine is an opiate medicine used to relieve pain, so it is a painkilling medication.

clue.text: Black bird in wood

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: A dark bird perched among the trees of a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wood' looks like a forest for the bird to sit in; it is the definition, from the game of bowls, where the balls are called woods.
explanation.definitionFit: In lawn bowls each ball rolled is called a wood, after the material the balls were once made from.

clue.text: Sample crumbly mince pies, leaving one

indicators.note: something crumbly falls to pieces, so these letters break up and re-form
one is a single letter I, and leaving means it walks out of the fodder

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An invitation to taste some crumbly festive pastries, though one has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one I from MINCE PIES, then rearrange the remaining eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen is a single example taken to show what the whole is like, which is what a sample is.

clue.text: Contradicted necessity to carry gun

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it inside, so one word is placed within the other

parts.note: a need is a necessity
gat is old American slang for a pistol

explanation.surface: Someone argued against the idea that you have to carry a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate a statement is to deny it or declare it untrue, which is to contradict it.

clue.text: See occupational therapist in French resort

indicators.note: one thing being in another means the first is placed inside the second

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera
OT is the standard abbreviation for occupational therapist

explanation.surface: An instruction to visit a therapist who is based on the Riviera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like an instruction to visit; it is the verb meaning observe.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice something is to become aware of it with the eyes, the everyday sense of see.

clue.text: Pretty useful member of search party?

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, so read as 'a pretty one'

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: someone skilled at searching

explanation.surface: Someone saying a person on a rescue team was rather handy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty useful' reads as 'fairly helpful'; split it, and the second half breaks the answer into its parts literally.
explanation.definitionFit: An attractive person is called a good-looker, and taken literally the phrase describes someone skilled at hunting for things.

clue.text: Flirt from Liechtenstein seen in German city

indicators.note: something seen in a place is inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Trier is an old city in western Germany
FL is the international vehicle code for Liechtenstein

explanation.surface: A playboy from a tiny Alpine principality spotted in a German town.
explanation.definitionFit: A trifler toys with people's affections without serious intent, which is what a flirt does.

clue.text: Offence perpetrated by Alexander against Diogenes?

definitions.text: Offence perpetrated by Alexander against Diogenes?

parts.words: Offence perpetrated by Alexander against Diogenes?
parts.note: surface reading: some crime the conqueror committed against the philosopher
setter's reading: in the story, Alexander the Great asked Diogenes what he wanted, and was told to stand out of his sunlight

explanation.surface: A historian asking what crime the great conqueror committed against the philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: Diogenes, sunbathing, asked Alexander the Great to move because he was blocking the sun; the phrase for gross overcharging is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a blatant swindle, read literally, means stealing someone's sunshine, as Alexander did.

clue.text: Financial provision, with grounds for some assurance?

parts.words: Financial provision, with grounds for some assurance?
parts.note: surface reading: a money arrangement backed by good reasons for confidence
setter's reading: assurance is life insurance, and a legal ground is a basis written into it

explanation.surface: Someone describing a sound money plan that gives them reasons to feel secure.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain assurance means life insurance; this kind pays out a lump sum at a fixed date or on death.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a life insurance contract that also builds savings, so it is a long-term arrangement for money.

clue.text: Make improvements in diet, perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps says the word is only one possible arrangement of these letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about whether to improve one's eating habits.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit a text is to revise and correct it, making changes to improve it.

clue.text: Condiment, one Cilla served up with pilchard half submerged

indicators.note: food served up is prepared and dished out, so these letters are cooked into a new order
with half of it under water, only half of the word shows above the surface

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
the fish, of which only the front half survives

explanation.surface: Cilla is dishing up a pilchard half-sunk in a sauce, perhaps a relish.
explanation.walkthrough: Only PILC, the first half of pilchard, is kept; mixed with I and CILLA it gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Piccalilli is a bright yellow pickle of chopped vegetables in mustard sauce, eaten as a relish.

clue.text: They'll need space to manoeuvre in

definitions.text: They'll need space to manoeuvre in

parts.words: They'll need space to manoeuvre in
parts.note: surface reading: people who need plenty of room to move around
setter's reading: space is outer space, where these travellers operate

explanation.surface: Someone noting that certain people require lots of elbow room.
explanation.definitionFit: Space travellers carry out their manoeuvres beyond Earth's atmosphere, in outer space.

clue.text: Greek not so difficult? It's comparatively hard to grasp!

parts.note: GR is the abbreviation for Greek
less difficult means easier

explanation.surface: A student asks whether Greek is any less difficult, only to find it harder to master.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard to grasp' looks like difficult to understand; it means slippery to hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Something oilier is more slippery, so more difficult to keep hold of in the hand than something else.

clue.text: Constructed hut for quarter

indicators.note: something constructed is put together from parts, so these letters are assembled anew

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shack built to serve as living quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarter' looks like lodgings for the hut; it is the fraction.
explanation.definitionFit: One of four equal parts of something is a quarter of it, the fraction one in four.

clue.text: Given bun, dined out without being invited

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of its usual order, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A guest who ate a bun and dined out without any invitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming unbidden means arriving when nobody asked you to, unasked and uninvited by the host.

clue.text: Dominion's representative in Ireland

indicators.note: one thing being in another means the first is placed inside the second

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
an MP, Member of Parliament, is an elected representative

explanation.surface: A British colony's envoy posted to Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: An empire is a set of territories ruled by one power, and dominion means such a realm or rule.

clue.text: Coins North American pocketed, showing remorse

definitions.note: the answer is a noun; 'showing remorse' is the act that shows it

indicators.note: something pocketed is held inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: pence are British coins
NA is the abbreviation for North American

explanation.surface: An American who slipped some coins into a pocket feels guilty about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Penance is self-punishment undertaken to express sorrow for wrongdoing, a token of contrition.

clue.text: Grandparent possibly acting as an escort

definitions.note: 'possibly' marks a grandparent as one example

indicators.note: acting means playing a different part, so these letters take on a new role and order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly relative serving as someone's chaperone.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear in one's family line is any earlier generation, of which a grandparent is one example.

clue.text: Place for one of the sleeping partners?

definitions.text: Place for one of the sleeping partners?

parts.words: Place for one of the sleeping partners?
parts.note: surface reading: a sleeping partner is a business investor taking no active part
setter's reading: two people who share a room at night, each with a separate bed

explanation.surface: Someone asks where a silent investor in the firm should be seated.
explanation.walkthrough: A sleeping partner is the British term for an investor in a business who takes no part in running it.
explanation.definitionFit: One of a matching pair of single beds in a shared room, each for one of two people sleeping there.

clue.text: Following excerpt from Pasternak

indicators.note: an excerpt is a short piece taken from within a longer text

parts.note: the letters run inside the novelist's surname

explanation.surface: A passage from the Russian author of Doctor Zhivago comes next.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern means behind a vessel, so a ship coming along after another is following it.

clue.text: Status of occupier then, in past, maybe?

indicators.note: maybe says the words are only one possible arrangement of their letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A historian asks what a resident's standing was in former times.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenantship is the condition of holding a property as a tenant, the position of a person living there.

clue.text: Frenchman interrupts Liberal member

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something

parts.note: Lib is short for Liberal
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur

explanation.surface: A Frenchman heckles a Liberal Party MP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' looks like a member of parliament; it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: An arm or leg is a limb, and member is an old word for a part of the body.

clue.text: Small group taking time to go to S American resort

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian beach resort

explanation.surface: A few people taking a break to head for a South American beach town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To go to' tells you RIO follows T.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is a set of three, the smallest group bigger than a pair.

clue.text: Fridge in which there's double cream runs inefficiently?

definitions.note: a fridge is one example of the answer

indicators.note: something run inefficiently is badly organised, so these letters come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A faulty refrigerator in which the thick cream has gone runny.
explanation.walkthrough: Double cream is British for heavy cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Household appliances expected to last for years, like refrigerators and washing machines, are classed as long-lasting goods.

clue.text: Tramples over family member

definitions.note: this sense is a phrase, read as two words
definitions.meaning: first meaning, split in two: treads upon
second meaning: a spouse's son from an earlier relationship

explanation.surface: Someone walks all over a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words and it describes treading on something.
explanation.definitionFit: A son of one's husband or wife by a previous partner is a relation by marriage within the household.

clue.text: Danny craftily pocketing a couple of eggs? Twelve

indicators.note: pocketing something means holding it inside
doing something craftily means cunningly rearranging it, so the name's letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
an egg is shaped like the letter O, so two eggs give two Os

explanation.surface: Danny slyly pockets a pair of eggs at, it turns out, midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Noonday is the middle of the day, when the clock shows twelve o'clock.
